sources.title: Naga City Ordinance No. 2003-003, Section 6
sources.note: Enacted January 15, 2003. Lists the Ateneo de Naga main building with its old wooden classrooms and wooden faculty house for preservation; only the main building is mapped here (owner decision, October 9, 2026).

sources.title: Philippine Registry of Cultural Property (NCCA): Naga City entries
sources.note: Inspected October 8, 2026. Ateneo de Naga main building, wooden classrooms and old wooden faculty house: local cultural property under Ordinance No. 2003-003.

sources.title: Dateline Ibalon: Ateneo de Naga University, 85 years of academic excellence in Bicol (June 2025)
sources.note: Archbishop Santos began the main building on diocesan land near the Cathedral; it and the Jesuit residence were nearing completion in December 1941, with a four-pillar facade, when war broke out and Japanese forces made it a prison camp.

sources.title: Dateline Ibalon: Ateneo's iconic wooden building falls silent (January 2026)
sources.note: Reports farewell rites on December 18, 2025 for the main building's wooden two-storey wings, which stood for more than eight decades and are being demolished for a new administration building. The map keeps the mapped outline; no end year is set until demolition is confirmed.

text.en: The Ateneo de Naga main building was listed for preservation by City Ordinance No. 2003-003.
Archbishop Santos began the main building on diocesan land near the Cathedral; with its four-pillar facade, it was nearly finished in December 1941.
World War II broke out before classes could move in, and Japanese forces turned the new building into a prison camp.
Farewell rites for its wooden two-storey wings were held on December 18, 2025, ahead of their demolition for a new administration building.
